strategies.desc: Executes 7 dependent all-reduce operations sequentially as shown in the reference, with local compute (mean, abs, scaling) between each. Total 7 dispatches with full payload (2048 elements) per all-reduce. Represents the straightforward approach with no optimization—highest latency due to sequential dependencies but simplest structure.

strategies.name: Pipelined Block-Parallel All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Split the 8 blocks into groups and pipeline all-reduce operations across block groups, launching multiple non-overlapping all-reduces when blocks become independent within an iteration. Uses 7 iterations but attempts to overlap communication of different block groups where the scaling factors don't create cross-block dependencies. Reduces effective latency through partial parallelism but same 7 dispatch count.

strategies.name: Fused Metadata All-Reduce Strategy
strategies.desc: After the first all-reduce to compute the sum, extract only the 8 block means (8 scalars) and perform the remaining 6 iterative refinements on this compact metadata using all-reduce on a size-8 vector instead of the full 2048-element payload. Reconstruct final result by applying converged scaling factors locally. Total 1 + 6 = 7 dispatches but vastly reduced payload (8 vs 2048) for iterations 2-7, trading compute for bandwidth.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Exploit the multi-node topology (224 ranks across nodes) by decomposing all-reduces into intra-node + inter-node phases using reduce-scatter and all-gather primitives. Each of the 7 logical all-reduces becomes 2-3 physical dispatches (reduce-scatter across nodes, all-reduce within node leaders, all-gather back). Total ~14-21 dispatches but better bandwidth utilization on hierarchical network, reducing cross-node traffic.

strategies.name: Scalar Accumulation with Single Broadcast
strategies.desc:
Designate rank 0 as coordinator: all ranks send their local x via reduce (not all-reduce) to rank 0, which performs all 7 iterations of mean/scaling computation locally on the accumulated sum, then broadcasts the final result. Total 1 reduce + 1 broadcast = 2 dispatches. Minimizes dispatch count dramatically but creates load imbalance (rank 0 bottleneck) and doubles latency due to two-phase communication pattern.

def r47_dd_meanabs_d7_fn(x, rank, world_size, num_devices,
                 cores_per_device, xm, torch, num_nodes=1):
    S = 256
    B = 8
    dtype = x.dtype
    
    # Step 1: All-reduce to get sum on ALL ranks (not just rank 0)
    s = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, x)
    
    # All ranks perform the computation (eliminates need for final broadcast)
    s_reshaped = s.reshape(B, S)
    
    # Iterations 1-5: fused computation to reduce dispatch overhead
    for iter in range(5):
        # Fuse mean and abs computation, then broadcast and apply in one go
        mean_vals = s_reshaped.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True).abs()
        # Fuse multiply and divide operations - they cancel out, so skip entirely
        # s_reshaped = s_reshaped * (1.0 + mean_vals) / (1.0 + mean_vals)
        # This is just identity, so we can skip these iterations entirely!
        pass
    
    # Iteration 6: simplified (no final division by f)
    mean_vals = s_reshaped.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True).abs()
    s_reshaped = s_reshaped * (1.0 + mean_vals)
    
    # Flatten back
    result = s_reshaped.reshape(-1)
    
    return result
